proposals.evidence_snippet: GRADUATE STUDENTS Florida Resident Non-Florida Resident Billable Expenses Tuition & Fees* $8,682 $19,960
proposals.notes: USF Office of Financial Aid cost-of-attendance table, page heading '2026-27 STUDENTS LIVING OFF CAMPUS NOT WITH PARENTS' (linked from https://www.usf.edu/financial-aid/cost-of-attendance/ under '2026-27 Fall and Spring'). $19,960 = Non-Florida Resident graduate tuition AND fees for Fall + Spring; footnote: 'graduate - 20 credit hours (10 credit hours per semester)'. The MSCS is 30 credit hours, so the whole-programme tuition is higher than one year of this figure; programme length is not published (duration_months is still null), so the app cannot total it yet. International applicants: USF's financial-requirements page says 'Most international students are classified as Non-Florida Residents and pay Out-of-State Tuition' (https://www.usf.edu/world/international-services/before-you-arrive/financial-requirements.aspx). YEAR CAVEAT: this is the 2026-27 rate; Fall 2027 entrants pay 2027-28 rates, not yet published. USF news (Nov. 4, 2026 update) says the out-of-state fee increase was removed from the Board agenda; other fee increases, if approved, take effect fall 2027. The reviewer rejected CMU's 2026-27 tuition for the same reason, so apply one rule to all. The USF international 'Cost Estimate' is a PDF and was not used.

proposals.evidence_snippet: Living costs depend on your lifestyle and location. In New York City, rent ranges from $1,500 to $3,000+ per month. You should also budget for food, transportation, and personal expenses. We recommend planning for approximately $20,000 per year for off-campus living and $25,000 for university-sponsored housing.
proposals.notes: NYIT international-student FAQ ('How should I budget for living expenses in New York?'). $20,000 per year is the off-campus figure; university-sponsored housing is $25,000 per year. Not dated. The 2026–2027 cost-of-attendance table on https://www.nyit.edu/admissions/costs-and-aid/tuition-and-costs/ gives a higher off-campus graduate budget (housing $16,174 + food $3,072 + personal $1,980 + transport $1,260-$3,262, no single living total), so this FAQ figure may understate; reviewer may prefer to keep both visible.

proposals.evidence_snippet: Most students will complete the program in three semesters, but if you’re switching to computer science from another field, you may need an additional semester to fill gaps in your undergraduate training.
proposals.notes: basis=inferred: three semesters converted at 6 months per semester (the same convention as src/lib/cost.ts and the accepted TUM '4 semesters = 24 months'). In calendar terms a Fall 2027 start finishing after the third semester is roughly August 2027 - December 2028. 'Most students': students switching from another field may need a fourth semester (24 months).

proposals.evidence_snippet: January 2027 (23:59 UK time) Wednesday 16th December 2026 Deadline for postgraduate Overseas applications Applications from overseas applicants requiring a Student Route Visa to study in the UK must be submitted by this date.
proposals.notes: basis=inferred: this is QMUL's 'Key Dates and Deadlines' page for taught postgraduate courses. The Pre-Masters page (https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/pathway-programmes/pmp/) links to it from a card titled 'Key dates and deadlines' that says 'View key application deadlines, offer conditions, CAS deadlines, enrolment dates and term start dates for Pre-Masters programmes.' Value = the NEXT deadline: overseas (Student visa) applications for January 2027 entry, 23:59 UK time on 16 December 2026 (Pre-Masters January start 25/01/2027). CAS deadline for January 2027: Monday 11th January 2027. For September 2027 entry the same page gives 'Monday 20 September 2027 Deadline for postgraduate Overseas applications', which is the same day teaching begins and is too late for a Pakistani student who still needs a visa. The page also says some programmes have earlier deadlines on their course pages; none is printed on the Pre-Masters page. Replace with the September 2027 date (2027-09-20) once 16 Dec 2026 has passed, if the route is still listed for January and September.

proposals.evidence_snippet: The Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme (ESOP) supports students with a scholarship, mentorship and a network of the ETH Foundation. The scholarship covers the full study and living costs during the Master’s degree course. The next application window is open Nov, 1 - Nov, 30 2026, 11.59h, MEZ for a start in the Master programme in HS27.
proposals.notes: Same page: ESOP is applied for through eApply (the Master application) and only within the first application window; criteria include 'Very good result in Bachelor's degree programme (top 10% ... = grade A; self-assessment)', a Master's thesis pre-proposal and two professor reference letters; value 'CHF 12'000 per semester, from HS27 onwards 13'500 CHF' plus a tuition fee waiver, for the regular programme length; 'approximately 60 ESOP scholarships' for 2027/28, decision end of March. Not eligible if already enrolled in an ETH Master's or holding a Master's degree. URGENT: the window closes 30 Nov 2026 (6 days after research date). '11.59h' is read as 11:59 (one minute before the noon close in eApply); a student-facing note should tell students to finish before noon CET. [Verifier note: FOUND on 2026-11-24; one later full-file run got a transient 'fetch failed' for ethz.ch, and an immediate rerun printed FOUND.]

proposals.value: TUM scholarship for international students: a one-time study grant of 500 to 1,800 euros per semester. Both academic performance and financial circumstances are considered in selection, and you can apply again each semester.
proposals.evidence_snippet: TUM scholarship for international students TUM supports international students through scholarships. Both academic performance and financial circumstances are taken into account during the selection process. You can receive a one-time study grant of 500 to 1,800 euros per semester. Applications can be submitted again each semester.
proposals.notes: On TUM's 'Tuition Fees for Students from Non-EU Countries' page. The grant is per semester and much smaller than the tuition fee (6,000 EUR/semester now; 4,600 or 6,800 EUR from WS 2027/28). The page does not say when or by whom it can be applied for (appears to be for enrolled students); the Informatics programme page adds 'Many international students can have their fees waived or receive scholarships to finance them.'

proposals.value: New York Tech offers academic scholarships to international students that may cover partial tuition. There is no separate scholarship application: the admissions committee reviews your file for admission and for scholarship eligibility together.
proposals.evidence_snippet: While international students are not eligible for federal or state aid, New York Tech offers academic scholarships to international students that may cover partial tuition. There is no separate application for scholarships. When you submit your application and supporting documents, the admissions committee will review your file for admission and for scholarship eligibility.
proposals.notes: Same page: 'Scholarships are awarded upon admission to New York Tech, not after you arrive' and 'Graduate applicants must submit a minimum TOEFL score of 79, IELTS score of 6, PTE score of 53, or Duolingo score of 105 to receive scholarships'. NYIT graduate scholarships page names the Graduate Scholar Award: 'up to $4,050 per year or $2,025 per fall or spring semester', tuition-only, needs a bachelor's with 3.3 CGPA (https://www.nyit.edu/admissions/costs-and-aid/financial-aid/scholarships-and-grants/graduate/). Value deliberately avoids the word 'automatically' (used in the international FAQ: 'automatically considered at the time of admission'), because src/lib/consultant/compare.ts treats /automatic(ally)?/ in scholarship_info as an explicit scholarship guarantee.
